sentences.text: In this appeal claimants 3 and 4 in LAR No.1 of 2022 of the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, Kottayam, is challenging the judgment dated 22.01.2025 by which the reference was answered against the claimants.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, Kottayam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. An extent of 1.50 Ares of property in Survey No.528/15-3 in Block No.28 of Athirampuzha Village,
Kottayam Taluk in Kottayam District was acquired from the appellants for the purpose of doubling of Railway Track.
Notification under Section 4(1) was published on 08.02.2019 and notification under Section 11(1) was published on 07.03.2020.
The award was passed on 09.11.2021 and the possession of the property was taken on 26.11.2021.
3. Dissatisfied with the amount granted as compensation by the Land Acquisition Officer, reference was sought.
LAR No.1 of 2022 was considered by Authority along with four other cases arising from the same acquisition.

4. The Authority considered the following points in LAR No.1 of 2022:
"1. Whether the claimant is entitled to get enhanced land value for the acquired property, if so, what should be the amount?
Whether the claimant is entitled to get enhanced compensation for structures and trees as claimed?

3.Reliefs and costs?"
5.
Finally the Authority answered the reference against the claimants.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants, the learned Senior Government Pleader appearing for the State and the learned Central Government Counsel appearing for the Railways.

7. During the course of hearing, the learned counsel for the appellants assailed the impugned Ashamol V vs State Of Kerala on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30156383/
2 judgment mainly on two grounds.

entities.text: Ashamol V vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. Taking exception to the conclusion by the learned Authority recorded in Paragraph No.24 of the impugned judgment, the learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the conclusion of the Authority is in conflict with the law laid down by a Division Bench of this Court in Aleyas K.C. v.
State of Kerala [2025 (1) KLT 747].

entities.text:
Aleyas K.C. v.
State of Kerala [2025 (1) KLT 747]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The next contention raised by the learned counsel for the appellants is regarding 12% increase under Section 30(3) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 being applied allegedly on land value instead of market value.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
9. The learned Authority refused to rely on the valuation in Ext.A1 Basic Valuation Report holding that the same is impermissible in LA.APP. NO. 190 OF 2025 5 2026:KER:8612 view of explanation 3 to Section 26 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: A Division Bench of this Court considered the scope and ambit of the explanation in Aleyas K.C.'s case.
It is apposite to refer to the following paragraph of the judgment of the Division Bench.
"42. A reading of Explanation 3 shows that what is prohibited is placing reliance on the compensation granted under the Act in similar case while determining the market value.
The component of compensation provided under the Act includes solatium and interest.
However, read as may be, we are not able to find out any restriction created by the statute in relying on the market value fixed by the reference court under the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act 1894.
Still further the word used is "amount paid as compensation" (emphasis supplied) and not the market value of the land.
The word 'compensation' mentioned in Explanation 3 to S.26(1) must be construed in the light of S.27 and S.28 of the Act.
A reading of S.28 shows that the Collector, in determining the compensation must take into account various components required by the Statute.
Pertinently, the market value is only one of the component of the compensation.

When the entire scheme of S.26 and S.28 is examined, it becomes evident that compensation determined under S.27 includes multiple factors mentioned under S.28, and therefore the parliament wanted to exclude the same and hence Explanation 3 was inserted.

To read Explanation 3 to S.26(1)(b) of the Act as one prohibiting the court to take into consideration the market value fixed by the reference court or High Court in respect of an acquisition in the same village at an earlier point of time would certainly amount to adding words into the statute which is impermissible going by settled principles governing Interpretation of Statute."
10.
In view of the law as explained by the Division Bench of this Court, the finding of the Authority recorded in Paragraph No.24 of the impugned judgment cannot be sustained.
Regarding the next issue raised by the learned counsel for the appellants, I find that the same was not at all considered by the Authority.

It is not clear from a reading of the impugned judgment Ashamol V vs State Of Kerala on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30156383/
3 as to whether the said issue was properly pointed out before the Authority.

entities.text: Ashamol V vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nevertheless, the said claim is a statutory claim and it cannot be ignored.
12. In view of the above, I am of the considered opinion that the reference requires fresh consideration by the Authority.
Therefore, I find that it is appropriate to set aside the impugned judgment and remit the matter for fresh consideration by the Authority.
13. In view of the above discussion, the impugned judgment in LAR No.1 of 2022 is set aside.
The Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, Kottayam, shall consider LAR No.1 of 2022 afresh.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, Kottayam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The learned Authority shall endeavour to pass judgment as early as possible since the acquisition is of the year 2019.
Appellants shall be entitled for refund the court fees.
Appeal is disposed of as above.
